items.prompt: In a partner webhook delivery system, an integration service must deliver a status change. the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates The design review focuses on iterative design communication and trade-off documentation. The same mechanism appears in a different domain with one constraint changed. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is make assumptions, rejected alternatives, and reversal evidence explicit during iterative design..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Make assumptions, rejected alternatives, and reversal evidence explicit during iterative design. In this transfer case for partner webhook delivery, a design can evolve when its decisions are tied to constraints and measurements rather than hidden intuition. The owner must also make a receiver that acknowledges late observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide iterative design communication and trade-off documentation independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a receiver that acknowledges late as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Make assumptions, rejected alternatives, and reversal evidence explicit during iterative design. It addresses the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates through an explicit mechanism and keeps a receiver that acknowledges late inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A design can evolve when its decisions are tied to constraints and measurements rather than hidden intuition. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For partner webhook delivery, the decision keeps the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a receiver that acknowledges late as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Iterative design communication and trade-off documentation” to terminology recall. Separate product requirements and quality targets from implementation choices; estimates must drive decisions rather than decorate the answer. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce iterative design communication and trade-off documentation must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Amazon SDE II Interview Prep (https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/sde-ii-interview-prep); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unowned_shortcut: It leaves iterative design communication and trade-off documentation dependent on caller discipline instead of placing the decision with the boundary that can enforce it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unbounded_scale: The extra mechanism may change consistency, duplicate work, or recovery behavior without addressing the decisive requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ignore_failure: A design answer must state what the user sees and who owns recovery when a receiver that acknowledges late occurs.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.provider_trivia: The architecture decision should survive a provider change; the mechanism and contract matter more than a product label.
